report.summary: Extended Jarvis's device-control capability with a third backed control, `dnd` (off/priority/alarms/none), generalising the existing `set_device_control` primitive rather than adding a new tool. A scheduled/condition automation or direct instruction can now set a named Do-Not-Disturb state via the system NotificationManager, with honest read-back so an ignored or permission-denied change is reported as failure, never a fake success.
report.evidence_reviewed: RUN_STATE.json / AGENTS.md / PLAN.md (sessions 47-50); the existing device-control seam in TorchController.kt (DeviceControlOp + object DeviceControl), DeviceAutomation.kt SetDeviceControl dispatch, ToolRegistry.kt (TOOL_SET_DEVICE_CONTROL definition + validation), TaskPlanParser/TaskPlanSerializer/HybridStepExecutor/TaskOrchestrator wiring, PlannerPromptBuilder ACTION_CATALOG, and the analogous TorchController/RingerModeController read-back implementations. CapabilityUpgradeTest DND tests.
report.findings: Confirmed (high confidence): the device-control seam was explicitly designed so a new control is a mapping plus a dispatch arm, never a new tool (AGENTS.md), and `dnd` was a queued roadmap item - the natural next increment toward the capability bar. Confirmed: `DeviceControl.resolve` already rejects unknown (control,value) pairs, so adding `dnd` needed only a resolver branch, an executor arm, DI, prompt wording and tests - low regression risk. Confirmed: DND is distinct from ringer mode (notifications vs ringing) and needs notification-policy access, which the platform enforces.
report.milestone_implemented: `dnd` device control. New `DndController`/`AndroidDndController` (NotificationManager.setInterruptionFilter + currentInterruptionFilter read-back + isNotificationPolicyAccessGranted pre-check), closed `DndMode` enum, `DeviceControlOp.Dnd` resolver branch, executor dispatch, application wiring, prompt catalogue wording, and AGENTS.md documentation. Advances the Top Priority bar by adding a real system-action capability (proactive 'go silent at night' automation) through the extensible control seam.
